## Summary

Updated the runtime-comparison artifact (same URL, ff9f4ee7) to reflect the TypeScript 7.0.2 upgrade shipped in 87c4619, and answered two follow-up questions in it: why people write CLIs in Rust or Zig if TypeScript is fine, and how sofar scales. Added the TS 7 finding as the lead item, a Compiler speed row to the matrix, and two sections. The CLI section reframes the question away from the CLI category toward four discriminators that ripgrep, fd, uv and ruff all answer the opposite way sofar does: whether users already have the runtime (sofar users all do, Claude Code requires Node), whether the work is CPU-bound (sofar folds 10,460 JSON records and waits on write), whether it runs in a hot loop (once per hook at 26ms, not per keystroke), and whether a library surface ships alongside (sofar ships three JS entry points plus a browser bundle). Supporting point: the JS ecosystem already split along exactly that CPU-bound line — esbuild, swc, oxc, ruff and now tsc 7 went native while npm, pnpm, wrangler and the Vercel CLI stayed JS, because orchestration waits on IO. The scalability section states the real ceiling rather than dismissing it: the fold is O(n) per invocation, roughly 20-25ms of work at 10,460 events once node boot is subtracted, so about 250ms at 100k and 2.5s at a million, and that ceiling arrives in any language. A rewrite buys a constant factor while the ceiling is algorithmic. Grounded in this repo's own prior finding, quoted from the header comment of core/index-tier1.ts: buildGraph re-derives the whole graph at ~16ms and growing with history, and the way out is not a faster graph build but a different shape — the persisted keyed index with INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION that turns sweeps into lookups. The scaling fix was already written in TypeScript and already shipped.

## Next action

Nothing outstanding on this initiative — close typescript-7 if you agree the upgrade is done.
